steps.note: Both train on 4 cards with the speech head off. LoRA + ZeRO-3: 10.5 GB per card, 3.5 s per step of 4 samples. QLoRA: 11.5 GB, 1.1 s. This showed LoRA fits on the 16 GB cards; MiniCPM-o still needs its own smoke test (step 10).
steps.title: Smoke test on Fun-Audio-Chat: LoRA + ZeRO-3 and QLoRA

steps.note: Main line moved to MiniCPM-o, which already runs in full duplex. Its duplex sequence is one unit per second of audio, with <|listen|> / <|speak|>, <|chunk_eos|> and <|turn_eos|>; the language model (Qwen3-8B) can take LoRA. Samples are stored model-neutral, so the data serves either model.
steps.title: Switch to MiniCPM-o 4.5: full-duplex format and LoRA feasibility

steps.note: 17,480 tools (When2Call 3,267, ToolACE 14,213); 126 FDB-like tools removed. The held-out split uses the domain labels from the next step.
steps.title: Tool pool and held-out tool split

steps.note: 17,397 labeled (83 dropped: answer outside the label set). 14,168 suit voice: 11,312 lookup, 1,515 search, 1,341 action. Held out six whole domains (health, food, calendar, weather, real_estate, jobs): 1,662 tools, 276 of them action; 12,506 tools left for training.
steps.title: Tool weight labels (lookup, search, action)

steps.note: Done: 154 batches written and checked, then three fix passes. Third pass (after the stratified review): dropped 996 samples that read API values aloud (Qwen3-14B proposed, Claude confirmed), all 427 first-round ask rewrites, 338 asks and 59 chats that failed a Claude review of every ask and chat, 7 card numbers and 5 reviewed leaks; added 835 new asks written and reviewed by Claude. Final set: 14,076 samples (train 12,686, dev 694, test 696); call 33.0%, handoff 31.0%, ask 15.7%, chat 10.6%, split 9.6%; 1,945 filler, 728 self-correction. Section C passes. Fourth pass (after the training-target review): split and handoff acknowledgments rewritten where they claimed a result or added details the user never gave (807 split, 1,076 handoff), 59 samples with a plain name in an ID argument dropped, and 78 backend results made failed or partial with an answer that says so. Final set: 14,017 samples (train 12,632, dev 690, test 695); Section C passes.
steps.title: Requests and targets (fast tools in the frontend, the rest handed off)

steps.note: Done with Kokoro (18 English voices, 16 kHz): every user turn of the 14,076 samples, earlier context turns included (22,955 WAVs, counting those of samples dropped afterwards). ISO dates read as spoken dates; one 0.5-2 s pause at a phrase boundary in 30% of requests.
steps.title: TTS, with pauses at phrase boundaries

steps.note: Format proven by the feasibility test (duplex target right 52-54/60 vs 20/60 untrained; results fed back as text units told with a value 30/34). Final training set built: the 14,017 samples in the new layout (acknowledgment spoken first, then the calls; speech at the model's own pace of about 3 tokens a second), plus 800 two-request episodes (a backend result arrives after the user asked something else): 14,817 sequences, 28 GB. Self-distillation keeps MiniCPM-o's own duplex behavior in the mix: 3,500 DailyDialog conversations run through the untrained model, 3,229 kept after dropping 202 that kept talking through a cut-in, 37 that never spoke and 32 that said it is Qwen. The training script mixes them, with learning-curve subsets.
steps.title: MiniCPM-o duplex format, training setup and smoke test

steps.note: Claude reviewed the 280-sample stratified review (target right 97.5%, fully correct 89.6%); you decided the four problem groups; the third fix round applied them to the whole set with a Claude review of every ask and chat and of every flagged API-value request. The final set passes section C.
steps.title: Your review of the data
Untrained MiniCPM-o baseline
steps.note: Done in text chat mode (full duplex has no tool-call path; TTS not run yet): official MiniCPM-o 4.5 code, fast tools + spawn_thinking, 692 test samples. Target accuracy 59.2%: call 61.2%, handoff 84.5%, ask 13.8%, split 49.3%, chat 62.4%. It over-hands-off (75 call and 25 chat items sent to the backend), almost never asks, and says nothing when it hands off (0 of 198). Reporting a backend result already works: 31/31 right after the handoff, 30/31 after an unrelated exchange. Full duplex on speech (695 test samples, result fed back): target right 142/695 (20.4%). Almost no tool calls: 30 items contain one, 22 of them unclosed. It says it will do the task, or asks, instead: 113 of 223 call items and 64 of 193 handoff items are talk only. Spoke before the user finished on 186. Of the 101 samples with a result it told the user on 39 and used a value on 31 (handoff 8/31). Behavior on 300 held-out conversations: 280 pass; 14 of 104 cut-ins kept speaking 3 s in, 4 never spoke, 2 said Qwen.
All four runs done. Dev loss 1.57 untrained, 0.460 at 12.5%, 0.431 at 25%, 0.414 at 50%, 0.399 at 100%.
